MAJOR: Binding open-question parity obligation unmet: no tests (Go or Python) for invalid non-integer `seq`, unknown `event_version`, or cursor ordering (`seq > cursor`); only missing-seq, envelope unknown-field, and signature are covered.

Unknown-field rejection parity is proven only for `event-envelope` in Python; subscription/alert-rule/webhook-delivery rejection is asserted in Go only, so cross-language shape parity for those three contracts is untested (AC risk).
Design guardrail "subscription contracts require tenant + auth_ref" only half-implemented: `tenant_id` made required in both mirrors while `auth_ref` remains optional.
MINOR: Go `ContractMetrics` is an exported mutable map while Python `CONTRACT_METRICS` is read-only; a silent mutation breaks metric-name parity with no Go-side assertion on `parity_failures` or labels.

`webhook_headers` emits `X-PF-Signature` with an empty value when the secret is empty; receivers treating header presence as authenticated can mis-handle it — omit or fail instead of emitting an empty signature.

Test names do not map to the design test_matrix names (`test_contracts_unknown_field_parity`, `test_contracts_seq_parity`, `test_contracts_subscription_alert_webhook_parity`, `test_webhook_hmac_constant_time`), weakening FR/traceability evidence.
NIT: `containsField` linear-scans the allowlist for every payload field (O(n·m)); a set/map would satisfy the allocation-light performance NFR.
`test_eventing_tenant_and_idempotency_contract` mixes tenant rejection, HMAC, and header assertions in one test, obscuring failure signals.
Python `webhook_signature`/`verify_webhook_signature` coerce inputs via `str()`/`bytes()` silently; a non-bytes body type is coerced rather than rejected, unlike Go's typed `[]byte`.
SUMMARY: Directionally correct: both Go mirrors updated in lockstep, constant-time fail-closed HMAC, extensions surface, and a named cross-language parity test exist. Top risks: approved binding test obligations (invalid seq, unknown version, cursor ordering) and the `auth_ref`-required invariant are not implemented, and unknown-field rejection parity is proven only for the event envelope.
